# 3.9 - Project: Feedback and Share {.unnumbered}

No real project is good the first time. People who write books, build bridges, and make apps all show their work early. They ask, "What is not working?" Then they make it better.

Today you get feedback from your classmates and from AI. You make your project better. Then you show it.

:::{.agenda}
**Today's Plan** (40 minutes)

- [🔥]{.icon} **Warm Up** Kind, specific, helpful [4 min]{.time}
- [👥]{.icon} **Learn Together** How to give feedback [6 min]{.time}
- [🛠️]{.icon} **Try It** Gallery walk, then make it better [18 min]{.time}
- [💬]{.icon} **Talk About It** Share your project [12 min]{.time}
:::

:::{.objectives}
- [ ] I can give feedback that is kind, specific, and helpful.
- [ ] I can use feedback to make my project better.
- [ ] I can compare feedback from people and feedback from AI.
- [ ] I can explain my project in one minute.
:::

::::{.vocab}
:::{.word-cards}
- [🗣️]{.icon} {{< glink feedback >}}: comments that tell you what is good and what to make better
- [🔁]{.icon} {{< glink revise >}}: to change your work to make it better
- [🖼️]{.icon} {{< glink "gallery walk" >}}: walking around the room to look at everyone's work and leave notes
- [👥]{.icon} {{< glink audience >}}: the people who will read, see, or use your work
:::
::::

:::{.guided-notes-link}
[Printable lesson sheet](/handouts/Unit_3/3.9_Project_Feedback_and_Share.pdf){target="_blank"} - feedback notes and your share plan.
:::

{{< warmup >}}

Which feedback helps more? Why?

1. "It's good."
2. "The price on your flyer is easy to see. The date is very small. Maybe make it bigger?"

:::{.think title="The second one"}
The first one is kind, but you cannot do anything with it. The second one is **kind**, **specific** (the price, the date), and **helpful** (make it bigger). You know exactly what to change.
:::

{{< learn >}}

### 3.9.1 - Kind, Specific, Helpful

| Not helpful | Helpful |
|---|---|
| "It's bad." | "I could not find the deadline. Can you put it at the top?" |
| "Nice." | "Your study guide has great examples. The quiz needs answers." |
| "I don't get it." | "I did not know who this is for. Maybe add a title?" |

Use these starters on your notes:

:::{.frames}
- **I like** ... because ...
- **I wonder** ...
- **What if** you ... ?
:::

***

### 3.9.2 - People and AI Give Different Feedback

| Feedback from AI | Feedback from people |
|---|---|
| fast, any time | takes more time |
| does not know you, your family, or our school | knows you and the people who will use it |
| may say "Great job!" too easily | can tell you if it is really useful |
| good at spelling and grammar | good at "Would I really use this?" |

The best projects use both.

{{< tryit >}}

### 3.9.3 - Gallery Walk

:::{.steps}
1. Put your product, plan, and prompt log on your desk.
2. Walk to another project. Read it. Leave a sticky note: **I like**, **I wonder**, or **What if**.
3. Visit **3 projects**. Every project should get at least 3 notes.
4. Go back to your project. Read your notes.
:::

:::{.gotcha title="Class size"}
**Small class (4 or 5):** sit in a circle. Pass your project to the right. Write a note. Keep passing until everyone has read every project. **Big class:** 3 rounds of 4 minutes. Mr. Ross says when to move.
:::

### 3.9.4 - Make It Better

Work with your project partner.

:::{.steps}
1. Ask your class AI tool for feedback too. Use the feedback prompt from Lesson 3.3.
2. On your sheet, compare: what did people say? What did AI say?
3. Choose the **2 most useful** pieces of feedback. Change your project.
4. Write what you changed in your prompt log.
:::

{{< talk >}}

### 3.9.5 - Share Your Project

Each pair shares for **one minute**. Use your sheet to plan.

:::{.frames}
- Our problem was ...
- We made ...
- AI helped us by ...
- We checked ... and we found ...
- We did ... ourselves.
- After feedback, we changed ...
:::

:::{.gotcha title="Class size"}
**Small class:** everyone shares to the whole class. **Big class:** share in groups of 3 pairs at the same time. Each group picks one project to share with the whole class.
:::

{{< further >}}

:::{.project title="A Real Audience"}
Share your product with the people it is for: your family, another class, a coach, or the ELL teachers. Ask them: "Is this useful?" What did they say?
:::

:::{.project title="How We Used AI"}
Make a class poster: one box for each project. In each box: the problem, one great prompt, and one mistake the AI made that you caught.
:::
